claim: Pembrolizumab improves survival as second-line therapy in advanced gastric cancer
gold_rationale: The directly on-point pivotal RCT, KEYNOTE-061 (Shitara, Lancet 2018; NCT02370498), randomized pretreated advanced gastric/GEJ cancer patients with PD-L1 CPS>=1 to pembrolizumab vs paclitaxel as SECOND-LINE therapy and FAILED its co-primary overall-survival endpoint: median OS 9.1 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.66-1.03), one-sided p=0.0421 against a prespecified threshold of 0.0135 — i.e., no significant OS benefit. PFS actually favored paclitaxel (HR 1.27). The only positive pembrolizumab monotherapy data in pretreated gastric cancer came from KEYNOTE-059 cohort 1 (Fuchs, JAMA Oncol 2018; NCT02335411), a single-arm phase 2 measuring the SURROGATE endpoint objective response rate (11.6% overall, 15.5% in PD-L1+), which supported a 2017 FDA accelerated approval in the third-line-plus setting — not an OS demonstration. That accelerated approval was voluntarily WITHDRAWN by Merck effective 2021 in consultation with the FDA after the confirmatory requirement to show an OS benefit in a phase 3 study was not met (ODAC voted 6-2 to withdraw on 29 April 2021; Merck announced withdrawal 1 July 2021). KEYNOTE-062 (Shitara, JAMA Oncol 2020; NCT02494583) further showed first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy was only non-inferior — not superior — to chemotherapy for OS. Across the randomized evidence, single-agent pembrolizumab has never demonstrated a statistically significant OS improvement as second-line therapy in PD-L1+ advanced gastric cancer, and the corresponding US indication was withdrawn. Clinical/regulatory consensus: Not Supported.
population: pretreated PD-L1+ (CPS>=1) advanced gastric / gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma
provenance: Verified independently: PMIDs 29880231, 29543932, 32880601 confirmed via PubMed metadata (titles, designs, N, effect sizes, article types — none retracted). NCT02370498 confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov (phase 3, OS/PFS co-primary, second-line, completed). 2021 withdrawal confirmed via Merck press release (1 Jul 2021) and corroborated by FiercePharma, CancerNetwork, BioCentury, TargetedOnc, pharmaphorum (ODAC 6-2 on 29 Apr 2021).

rows.citation: Shitara K, et al. Pembrolizumab versus paclitaxel for previously treated, advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer (KEYNOTE-061): a randomised, open-label, controlled, phase 3 trial. Lancet. 2018;392(10142):123-133. DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(18)31257-1 (NCT02370498).
rows.finding: Pivotal SECOND-LINE phase 3 in exactly the claimed population (PD-L1 CPS>=1 advanced gastric/GEJ). Pembrolizumab vs paclitaxel MISSED the OS primary endpoint: median OS 9.1 vs 8.3 mo, HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.66-1.03), one-sided p=0.0421 vs prespecified 0.0135 threshold — no significant OS benefit. PFS favored paclitaxel (HR 1.27). Directly contradicts the claim. VERIFIED: PubMed abstract confirms all figures; article types include 'Randomized Controlled Trial'/'Clinical Trial, Phase III'; NOT retracted.
rows.integrity_note: MSD-funded but negative for sponsor; endpoint prespecified; not retracted. Independently re-verified against PubMed.

rows.citation: Fuchs CS, et al. Safety and Efficacy of Pembrolizumab Monotherapy in Patients With Previously Treated Advanced Gastric and Gastroesophageal Junction Cancer: Phase 2 KEYNOTE-059 Trial. JAMA Oncol. 2018;4(5):e180013. DOI:10.1001/jamaoncol.2018.0013 (NCT02335411).
rows.finding: Single-arm, open-label phase 2 (cohort 1), third-line-plus. Primary endpoint was ORR (11.6% overall; 15.5% in PD-L1+), a SURROGATE — not OS. This ORR/durability read-out was the basis for the 2017 FDA accelerated approval, but it does not establish a survival benefit and has no comparator arm. VERIFIED: PubMed article type is 'Clinical Trial, Phase II'; abstract explicitly states 'single-arm, multicohort'.
rows.integrity_note: CORRECTED design tag from 'rct' to 'prospective cohort' — this is a single-arm phase 2 with no randomization/control, mapped to the least-wrong available enum. Outcome is surrogate ORR, not the claimed OS endpoint (direction 0).

rows.citation: Shitara K, et al. Efficacy and Safety of Pembrolizumab or Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy vs Chemotherapy Alone for First-line, Advanced Gastric Cancer: KEYNOTE-062 Phase 3 RCT. JAMA Oncol. 2020;6(10):1571-1580. DOI:10.1001/jamaoncol.2020.3370 (NCT02494583).
rows.finding: First-line phase 3 RCT (NOT second-line, so population mismatch on line of therapy). Pembrolizumab monotherapy was NON-INFERIOR but not superior to chemotherapy for OS in CPS>=1 (10.6 vs 11.1 mo, HR 0.91, 99.2% CI 0.69-1.18). Corroborates that single-agent pembrolizumab does not deliver an OS improvement over standard therapy in advanced gastric cancer. VERIFIED via PubMed; N=256 monotherapy arm confirmed.
rows.integrity_note: Different line of therapy from the claim (population_match=false is honest, not a suppressed contradiction — first-line does not contradict the second-line claim). Included for consistency of the OS evidence picture.

rows.citation: KEYNOTE-061: A Phase III, Randomized, Open-label Trial of Pembrolizumab (MK-3475) Versus Paclitaxel in Advanced Gastric/GEJ Adenocarcinoma Progressed After First-Line Platinum + Fluoropyrimidine. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02370498.
rows.finding: Registry record for the pivotal second-line trial confirming design (phase 3, randomized 1:1 pembrolizumab vs paclitaxel, co-primary endpoints OS and PFS in PD-L1 CPS>=1 participants) — independent verification of the KEYNOTE-061 primary source. VERIFIED via ClinicalTrials.gov: status COMPLETED, enrollment 592, has_results=true, OS listed as primary outcome in PD-L1 positive participants.
rows.integrity_note: Trial registry cross-check of the negative pivotal RCT. Re-verified directly against ClinicalTrials.gov.

rows.citation: Merck. Merck Provides Update on KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) Indication in Third-Line Gastric Cancer in the US. News release, Business Wire, 1 July 2021. (Underlying: FDA ODAC 6-2 vote to withdraw, 29 April 2021.)
rows.finding: Regulatory consensus row: the FDA accelerated approval for single-agent pembrolizumab in pretreated PD-L1+ (CPS>=1) gastric/GEJ cancer (granted Sep 2017 on ORR from KEYNOTE-059) was voluntarily WITHDRAWN in 2021 because the post-marketing requirement to demonstrate an OS benefit in a phase 3 trial was not met (confirmatory KEYNOTE-061/062 failed to show significant OS improvement). ODAC voted 6-2 to withdraw on 29 Apr 2021; Merck announced withdrawal 1 Jul 2021. Confirms the OS-benefit claim is Not Supported at the regulatory level.

baseline.text: No. Pembrolizumab does not have proven overall-survival benefit as second-line therapy in advanced gastric cancer. The pivotal phase 3 KEYNOTE-061 trial compared pembrolizumab to paclitaxel in previously treated PD-L1 CPS>=1 gastric/GEJ cancer and MISSED its overall survival primary endpoint (median OS 9.1 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.82, p=0.0421, not crossing the 0.0135 significance threshold); PFS even favored paclitaxel. The earlier accelerated approval was based on the single-arm KEYNOTE-059 study using objective response rate (a surrogate), not survival, and that third-line accelerated approval was voluntarily withdrawn in 2021 after failing to confirm an OS benefit. So the claim is Not Supported for second-line therapy.
